A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ARC-JSD and retain matching methods, experiments and appendices. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete documents, including their figures and tables.

before.justification: v3 reports original attribution experiments on three QA benchmarks, mechanistic analyses, component ablations and hallucination-gating results.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and reports additional backbone evaluations, individual-component ablations, token-level analyses and domain case studies.

M1.justification: Sentence-ablation JSD scoring, Logit Lens component ranking, semantic gains and the confidence-gating formula remain unchanged. The additional backbone evaluations and expanded source rankings do not document an algorithmic adaptation.

E1.justification: The three principal QA benchmarks remain unchanged. v5 Appendix J adds two medical and two legal QA cases, naming PubMedQA, MedQuAD and LegalBench as sources. This extends domain coverage through examples, without adding comprehensive domain benchmark evaluations.

E2.justification: ALTI-Logit, MIRAGE and Contextcite with 32 or 256 calls remain the benchmark comparators, including for the additional backbones. KL, TV, Wasserstein and MMD comparisons and the random masking/gating controls are also retained.

E3.justification: v5 adds MuSiQue evaluations with LLaMA-3.1-8B-IT and Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-IT. It also introduces individual-component ablation measured by attribution-accuracy decrease. Existing benchmark sampling, sentence-level accuracy evaluation and reported dataset sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's aggregate masking and gating studies, v5 adds individual attention-head and MLP ablations using accuracy loss (Figure 4), token-level JSD analyses (Figure 5), expanded multi-hop source rankings and four medical/legal cases (Appendices I–J). These substantially expand the mechanistic and case-study analyses.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same significance indicators, and Table 5 retains the same uncertainty reporting. Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts, and v5 introduces no additional uncertainty-estimation or statistical-testing practice.

E6.justification: v5 adds component-ablation outcomes, token-level findings, ranked-source scores and additional-backbone results; Figure 7 reports approximately 80% and 89% ARC-JSD accuracy for LLaMA and Qwen3-Next respectively. Existing ARC-JSD points also change: Hotpot QA Gemma2-9B moves from just below 80% to just above 80%, while TyDi QA Qwen2-7B and Gemma2-2B decrease. These revisions align with the retained metric-ablation plots; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

T1.justification: The scoring equations, semantic-gain and consensus definitions, Transformer derivations and TV counterexample are retained. v3 Appendix J becomes v5 Appendix L without substantive changes to its mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: efficient inference-time attribution, mechanistic localization and hallucination mitigation through component gating. Although v5 removes the conclusion section, its substantive claims remain elsewhere.

C2.justification: v5 Section 8 newly interprets ranked multi-hop sources as potentially revealing reasoning paths and discusses broader backbone and domain applicability. The low-JSD interpretation and Appendix C limitations concerning neuron-level analysis and other tasks remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 1 removes the explicit 'key-value caching' qualifier from ARC-JSD, reducing implementation disclosure without establishing a procedural change. Appendix E retains the H100 hardware, NLTK preprocessing and prompt templates. The new reproducibility statement repeats the existing code address.

R1.justification: v5 adds citations to Wang et al.'s Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Conversational Systems and Zeng et al.'s Affective Decoding for Empathetic Response Generation. Positioning against ContextCite, corroborative attribution and retrieval-head research remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained with localized editing. v5 converts Section 5's numbered subsections into paragraph headings, removes the conclusion, adds ethics/reproducibility/LLM-use statements and reorganizes appendix lettering. These are limited structural changes rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v5 adopts the ICLR layout, substantially shrinks and wraps Figure 3, and adds the component-ablation, token-JSD and additional-backbone figures. Appendix examples gain gold-answer and ranked-source panels, alongside new medical/legal displays. Existing heatmaps and metric-comparison figures are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The individual-component accuracy ablation and additional-backbone comparison strengthen empirical support beyond v3's existing validation. Revised benchmark points also resolve discrepancies with the retained metric-ablation plots. These are useful but limited gains: the domain extension consists of four cases, and source rankings alone do not establish the newly suggested reasoning-path interpretation.
